title: Companion gravity changes ASASSN-14ko passage times and tidal depths in two circular binary examples
abstract: We test the companion gravity omitted from two circular binary light-time fits to ASASSN-14ko. We integrate 80 restricted three-body examples for about 19 observer years. The active black hole has 10 million solar masses. The initial stellar radial period is 108.44 observer days and nominal eccentricity is 0.9. We vary mutual inclination, phase and pericentre direction, with and without central relativistic precession. After a free quadratic and outer-frequency sinusoid are removed, central-precession tracks leave timing RMS of 0.99-4.07 days for the shorter binary fit and 0.12-0.75 day for the longer fit. All 78 tracks that complete the span have a pericentre range above 13 percent of the initial distance. Two Newtonian tracks reach an inner model boundary. Small timing residuals can coexist with large changes in tidal depth. A Roche size check alone does not test these effects. These are model calculations, not a fit to observed epochs or a binary exclusion. A sparse grid, fixed active mass, massless star, fixed initial period and incomplete relativistic force limit the scope. Code, aggregate inputs, simulated results and numerical checks are provided.
